who_what.text: The official README presents Hillock as a local memory engine with Python, CLI, and OpenAI-compatible FastAPI interfaces; local Ollama rendering is optional.
The reviewed code combines a SQLite graph, Hebbian association storage, and a hyperdimensional reservoir in IntegratedHillock.

architecture.text: SQLite stores entity records, subject-predicate-object relations, Hebbian weights, aliases, and compact document reservoir blobs; relations carry source-document labels, confidence, and creation time.

IntegratedHillock links query entities, fetches candidate triples, applies hypervector and predicate checks, and renders passing facts; the graph store, plasticity engine, and reservoir are composed as separate modules.
Document ingestion reads text or PDF within the project directory, routes text through TALON, writes extracted relations, and stores bound multi-hop path vectors keyed by document basename.

behavior.text: The relation batch writer ensures endpoint entities exist and performs inserts/replacements transactionally. Configured single-valued predicates remove an existing subject-predicate value before inserting its replacement.

Correction paths include explicit relation replacement, pronoun-fact removal followed by human-disambiguated insertion, entity merge with relation/association migration, and whole-database reset. These do not establish backup or replica erasure.

Recall links query strings to entity identifiers, fetches relations touching them, then scores candidates by hypervector similarity and predicate alignment before choosing facts for response rendering.
Hebbian updates strengthen co-active entity pairs and decay inactive pairs; association lookup can prime related concepts during answering.
The inspected API initializes one engine/database instance, exposes OpenAI-style chat responses and streaming, and returns zero-valued token usage fields rather than measured usage.

metrics.domain: Answerable retrieval, abstention, and negative controls
metrics.evidence: The fact gate and refusal paths were inspected; no answerable or unanswerable queries were run or scored.
Overwrite, disambiguation, alias, and merge paths were inspected; no correction probes were run.
Targeted row/entity deletion and reset paths exist; no post-deletion probes or backup/copy checks were run.
The inspected schema has no tenant or project key and the API creates one engine instance; no cross-scope workload was executed.
Source labels and renderer prompts were inspected; no output claims were adjudicated against stored source passages.
Source includes timing instrumentation and upstream timing claims; this review collected no runtime timing samples.
API token usage is hard-coded to zero and no provider charge or persistent storage measurement was collected.

limits.text: The relation schema records a source label, confidence, and timestamp but does not retain evidence spans, a trust state, or a mutation history.
Relation correction and entity merge are implemented, but full erasure from backups, external copies, or downstream consumers was not established.
No tenant, project, or user key appears in the inspected schema, and no authentication layer appears in the inspected API source; multi-user isolation is not established.
The README describes extraction throughput, memory footprint, similarity latency, and refusal behavior; those statements are upstream claims and were not reproduced.
Extraction quality, retrieval accuracy, abstention, citation support, and model behavior remain unknown because no runtime workload was run.

benchmark.note: No Hillock runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was run. Source observations and upstream README claims are not Hillock benchmark results.
